q: A 120 V circuit supplies a 10 Ω resistive load. What current flows?
A 240 V, single-phase resistive heater draws 20 A. What is its power?
A 1,200 W heating element is rated for 120 V. What is its resistance?
Resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω, and 30 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
explain: Series resistances add: 10 + 20 + 30 = 60 Ω.

q: Two 30 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
explain: Equal resistors in parallel: R / n = 30 / 2 = 15 Ω.

q: A 10 Ω and a 20 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
Resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω, and 30 Ω in series are connected across 120 V. What is the voltage across the 30 Ω resistor?
explain: Total R = 60 Ω, so I = 120 / 60 = 2 A. Voltage across 30 Ω = 2 × 30 = 60 V.

q: At any junction in a circuit, the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving. This is:
explain: Kirchhoff's current law: charge is conserved at a node. The voltage law says voltage drops around a closed loop sum to the source voltage.

q: A sine-wave voltage reads 120 V RMS on a meter. What is its approximate peak value?
A 60 Hz AC supply completes how many full cycles in one second?
explain: Hertz = cycles per second. 60 Hz = 60 cycles each second (120 alternations).

q: An AC circuit has 30 Ω of resistance and 40 Ω of inductive reactance in series. What is the impedance?
explain: Z = √(R² + X²) = √(900 + 1,600) = √2,500 = 50 Ω. Resistance and reactance add as vectors, not arithmetically.

q: A motor circuit uses 2,400 W of true power while drawing 3,000 VA of apparent power. What is the power factor?
A 240 V single-phase load draws 25 A. What is the apparent power?
A balanced three-phase, 208 V load draws 30 A per line at unity power factor. What is the power?
On a 480Y/277 V system, what is the relationship between 480 V and 277 V?
choices: 277 V is half of 480 V plus a safety margin
277 V is the delta phase voltage
explain: In a wye, line-to-line voltage = line-to-neutral × 1.732. 480 / 1.732 ≈ 277 V.

q: In a balanced delta-connected load, line current equals:
explain: Delta: line voltage = phase voltage, line current = √3 × phase current. Wye is the reverse.

q: A transformer steps 480 V down to 120 V. What is its turns ratio (primary:secondary)?
explain: Voltage ratio equals turns ratio: 480 / 120 = 4, so 4:1.

q: A 10 kVA single-phase transformer has a 240 V secondary. What is the full-load secondary current?
A 25 kVA three-phase transformer has a 208Y/120 V secondary. What is the full-load secondary line current?
One horsepower is equal to approximately how many watts?
explain: 1 hp = 746 W. A 5 hp output is about 3,730 W.

q: A 5 hp motor operates at 85% efficiency. What is its approximate input power?
explain: Output = 5 × 746 = 3,730 W. Input = output / efficiency = 3,730 / 0.85 ≈ 4,388 W.

q: A 120 V single-phase branch circuit runs 100 ft (one way) on 12 AWG copper (6,530 cmil) and carries 16 A. Using K = 12.9, what is the approximate voltage drop?
explain: VD = 2 × K × I × L / CM = 2 × 12.9 × 16 × 100 / 6,530 ≈ 6.3 V (about 5.3% — above the 3% branch-circuit recommendation).

q: The NEC informational note recommends limiting branch-circuit voltage drop to what percentage for reasonable efficiency of operation?
explain: Recommendation (not a requirement): 3% on the branch circuit and 5% total for feeder plus branch circuit.

q: If the length of a conductor is doubled (same material and size), its resistance:
explain: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

q: In a 120/240 V single-phase, 3-wire circuit, line A carries 20 A and line B carries 14 A. What does the neutral carry?
explain: On a single-phase 3-wire system the neutral carries the unbalance: 20 − 14 = 6 A.

q: In a perfectly balanced three-phase, 4-wire wye system supplying linear loads, the neutral current is:
explain: Balanced three-phase currents are 120° apart and cancel in the neutral. Nonlinear (harmonic) loads can change that.

q: If the frequency applied to an inductor increases, its inductive reactance:
explain: XL = 2πfL — reactance rises with frequency. Capacitive reactance does the opposite.

q: As frequency increases, the capacitive reactance of a capacitor:
explain: XC = 1 / (2πfC) — higher frequency, lower reactance.

q: A 1,500 W heater runs 8 hours a day for 30 days. At $0.15 per kWh, what does it cost?
As the temperature of a copper conductor rises, its resistance:
explain: Copper has a positive temperature coefficient. This is why ampacity tables carry temperature correction factors.

q: Three 60 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
explain: Equal resistors in parallel: 60 / 3 = 20 Ω.

q: A current of 5 A flows through an 8 Ω resistor. How much power is dissipated?
Two 20 Ω resistors in parallel are connected in series with a 10 Ω resistor across 120 V. What is the total current?
explain: Parallel pair = 10 Ω; total = 10 + 10 = 20 Ω; I = 120 / 20 = 6 A.

q: A wattmeter connected to an AC circuit measures:
explain: A wattmeter responds to voltage × current × power factor — true power. VA requires separate voltage and current readings.

q: A voltage is induced in a conductor when it:
choices: Cuts through magnetic lines of force
explain: Faraday's law of induction — the basis of generators and transformers. Relative motion (or changing flux) between conductor and field induces voltage.

q: A three-phase, 208 V load draws 50 A per line. What transformer kVA is needed (minimum, at full load)?
In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:
choices: Is in phase with the voltage
explain: ELI the ICE man: in an inductor (L), voltage (E) leads current (I); in a capacitor (C), current leads voltage.

q: A 7.2 kW resistive heater operates at 240 V single-phase. What current does it draw?
The DC resistance of 1,000 ft of 12 AWG uncoated copper at 75°C is approximately:
explain: Chapter 9, Table 8 lists roughly 1.9–2.0 Ω per 1,000 ft for 12 AWG copper. Each three sizes smaller roughly doubles the resistance.

q: A motor delivers 10 hp while drawing 9 kW from the line. What is its efficiency?
In a wye-connected load, the line current is:
explain: Wye: line current = phase current; line voltage = √3 × phase voltage.

q: A 15 kVA single-phase load at 240 V draws what current?
A three-phase, 480 V feeder runs 250 ft on 1/0 AWG copper (105,600 cmil) at 100 A. Using K = 12.9, the approximate voltage drop is:
In a series circuit, which quantity is the same through every component?
explain: Only one path exists, so current is identical everywhere. Voltage divides across the components.
